_comment: T4 CALIBRATION CONDITIONS -- one entry per EXPERIMENTAL POINT in
targets_T4.json, so every run is comparable to a measurement rather than
to a round-number grid point.  Ion and neutron are calibrated SEPARATELY
(two designs, two theta vectors); this file holds both families and the
design generator is pointed at one family at a time.
DOSE RATE IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE SPLIT.  Neutron is ~1e-7 dpa/s and ion
is ~1e-3 dpa/s -- four orders of magnitude.  G is taken from the SOURCE
ROW where the database reports it, not rounded to the family nominal: a
point measured at 7e-4 is not a 1e-3 point, and L_hat (the dose-rate
sensitive parameter, top-2 in the T3 screening) responds to exactly this.
T_K is the ACTUAL temperature.  The -60 C ion shift is a data-side
plotting device and must never reach the simulator -- run_ensemble asserts
on T_eq, so do not add it here.
DOSE IS NOT 1.0.  Each condition carries the dose of its measurement
(neutron 15-32 dpa, ion 4-30 dpa).  run_ensemble takes --dose globally, so
the ion and neutron families must be run as SEPARATE campaigns with their
own --dose, or the dose field here must be threaded through. The per-point
dose is recorded so the comparison is unambiguous either way.
rho_d IS A PER-CONDITION OVERRIDE, not a sampled parameter (apply_theta
writes cond['rho_d'] verbatim).  It is left at 1e14 for the neutron family
-- the T3 value -- and exposed per ion point because the instruction is
explicitly that ion may take a different dislocation density and bias.
Z_i / Z_i_loop are SAMPLED parameters, so they differ between the ion and
neutron fits automatically by virtue of being separate calibrations; they
do not belong here.

I420.label: HT9 ion 420 C, 4 dpa, in-situ Kr+ (Zheng 2018)
